summary.headline: Simplex Castings posted record Q2 FY27 PAT of ₹7.64 crore (+36.98% YoY, 12.13% margin) and reiterated ~₹300 crore FY27 revenue guidance.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 13.71% YoY to ₹63.01 crore, with EBITDA up 32.12% to ₹12.75 crore and EBITDA margin up 282 bps to 20.23%. H1 FY27 revenue was ₹123.96 crore (+23.21%), EBITDA ₹24.26 crore (19.58% margin) and PAT ₹14.5 crore (+40.55%, 11.7% margin). Management kept FY27 guidance at ₹300 plus crore and said H2 margins should be similar to H1, while the railway mega wagon order has slipped to the next quarter. Capital WIP rose to ₹36.77 crore from ₹12.38 crore, with two of three fabrication sheds expected in Q4 FY27 and a ₹500 crore FY28 target.

segments.name: Steel (coke oven doors and spares)
segments.commentary: Management says it holds about 90–95% share of castings for current coke oven battery projects, and the niche coke oven door orders are cited as the driver of margin expansion. Four batteries are planned next year (Bokaro, Bhilai, two for IISCO), worth about ₹25–30 crore each.

segments.name: Power (fabrication)
segments.commentary: Thermal power fabrication orders from L&T and BHEL are cited; BHEL has approved Unit 1 for fabrication equipment orders. Management targets over ₹150 crore of turnover in power-plant heavy structures.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: RDSO approval received for railway bogies, but the mega wagon order (about 1 lakh wagons over 2.5–3 years) slipped from Jul–Sep to next quarter. Management targets railways at 30–40% of output over 2–3 years, with couplers, suspension tubes and ADI wedges as Plan B.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of around ₹300 crore plus retained; management says October and half of November are running better than H1.
H2 FY27 split guided at about 40% in Q3 and 60% in Q4.
FY27 EBITDA/PAT margins expected to be similar to H1 FY27 levels.
FY28 revenue target of ₹500 crore; management says current capex is sufficient for it.
Long-term PAT margin view: 8–10% is the conservative target, versus historical 7–8% peak; current 12% is described as an anomaly driven by order mix.
capex_capacity: Fabrication shop: structure capacity to rise from about 500 tons to 1,500 tons per month; equipment capacity from about 200 tons to 300–350 tons per month.
Three new sheds with cranes planned; two expected to be commissioned in FY27 (Q4), with the third completing about six months from now.
Current utilisation expected to reach 80–90% of existing capacity by next financial year.
Management says capex stays at the original plan of ₹25 crore; the balance of the ₹50 crore raise goes to working capital.
Receipt of about ₹100 crore fund raise from premier Indian funds (preferential allotment) was announced.
demand_pricing: Pending order book about ₹150 crore, with a further ₹100 plus crore in pipeline; major part to execute in FY27.
Average order execution period cited at 3–4 months; coke oven doors take 4–5 months and fabrication equipment 6–7 months.
Margin gains attributed to niche products (coke oven doors and spares) and outsourcing of small castings, which cut other expenses.
Coke oven door order from Brazil for two batteries is expected.
Inventory build-up attributed to inspection timing and expected to clear; in-process WIP estimated at about ₹80 crore as revenue scales.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹300 crore FY27 revenue guidance intact, and what is the H2 margin outlook given H1 commodity inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated ₹300 plus crore and said margins should be similar to H1, with H2 seasonally stronger as customer budgets release.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the visibility and working capital funding to bridge ₹330 crore versus the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Bill discounting via L&T and BHEL platforms is used until the preferential money arrives; order book is about ₹150 crore with ₹100 plus crore in pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the railway mega order delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the wagon order from Railways is delayed to next quarter, affecting wagon builders such as Titagarh and Texmaco first; Simplex benefits via bogie demand and smaller private orders, with Plan B in couplers, suspension tubes and ADI wedges.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PAT margin of 12% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 8–10% is the realistic range; historical PAT peaked at 7–8%, and the current level reflects an exceptional order mix and market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall and where is the inventory build-up coming from?
qa_highlights.answer: Smaller castings are now made by outside vendors, lowering other expenses; inventory rise is linked to inspection timing and WIP, expected to clear.

qa_highlights.question: What capacity will the capex add and when will it be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Structure capacity rises from 500 to 1,500 tons per month and equipment from 200 to 300–350 tons; two sheds are due in Q4 FY27, but existing gantries allow output before the sheds are ready.

risks_watch: Railway mega wagon order has slipped repeatedly (from Jul–Sep 2026 to next quarter); management says railway bogie volumes depend on its release.
FY27 revenue target requires H2 revenue about 50% above H1; working capital is tight until the preferential allotment and bill discounting are in place.
Capex commissioning is pushed to Q4 FY27, with full completion about six months away, which could limit FY28 capacity.
Management flagged unspecified external risks (war, political) and treated the defence business as small (10–15% of shipbuilding and defence ambitions).
Margin sustainability: the 12% PAT is viewed by management as an anomaly, and 8–10% is the guided normal range.
summary.management_tone: Confident on steel and power demand and on FY27 guidance, but cautious on margins and railways, where management repeatedly described the mega order as delayed and urged conservatism on PAT margin.
key_quotes: This quarter, we delivered the highest-ever quarterly PAT in the company's history.
Historically, PAT for the company, even in the best of the years, has been a maximum of 7% to 8%; that is the history of the company.
So, for the financial part, I would like Mr. Avinash to take it over from me, and I am available for the conference.
We should be conservative; between 8% to 10% is what normally would happen with a company like us.

financial_highlights.change: +36.98% YoY; margin +206 bps; highest-ever quarterly PAT

adds.what: Fabrication shed capacity: structure capacity from ~500 to 1,500 tons/month; equipment from ~200 to 300-350 tons/month, via three new sheds with cranes
Two of three new fabrication sheds expected to be commissioned in Q4 FY27

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of ~₹300 crore plus held (H1 was ₹123.96 crore, implying a steep H2 ramp of ~40% in Q3 and 60% in Q4), backed by a ₹150 crore pending order book plus ₹100 crore pipeline and new fabrication sheds, though the railway mega order slipped a quarter and the sheds land only in Q4 FY27.

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 13.71% YoY to ₹63.01 crore, with EBITDA up 32.12% and margin up 282 bps, driven by niche coke oven door orders and outsourcing of small castings cutting other expenses, not by volume. The brief names no one-off gain or loss in either quarter, but management calls the 12% PAT margin an anomaly against a guided 8–10% normal range, so part of the margin lift may not recur.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides H2 EBITDA/PAT margins similar to H1 (H1 EBITDA margin 19.58%, PAT 11.7%), but calls the 12% PAT an anomaly and sees 8-10% as the normal range, so expansion beyond H1 is unlikely.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two of three new fabrication sheds with cranes are expected in Q4 FY27 (structure capacity 500 to 1,500 tons/month), with the third about six months out, though the sheds are not yet commissioned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of ~₹300 crore plus needs H2 about 50% above H1 (H1 ₹123.96 crore), backed by ₹150 crore pending order book plus ₹100 crore pipeline and October running ahead of H1 pace.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation expected to reach 80-90% of existing capacity by next financial year, but management says capex stays at the original ₹25 crore plan and FY28 ₹500 crore target is covered by current capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only reiterated ~₹300 crore plus FY27 guidance and kept H1-level margins, with railway mega wagon order slipped a quarter and working capital tight.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 needs H2 revenue about 50% above H1 while the railway mega wagon order (about 1 lakh wagons) has slipped from Jul-Sep to next quarter and working capital is tight until the ₹100 crore preferential money arrives.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Couplers, suspension tubes and ADI wedges are named as Plan B for railways, but no launch date was given; Brazil coke oven door order for two batteries is expected.

rows.label: Steel coke oven battery projects
rows.why: Four batteries planned next year (Bokaro, Bhilai, two for IISCO) at about ₹25-30 crore each, with Simplex holding about 90-95% of castings share.

rows.label: Railway mega wagon order
rows.why: About 1 lakh wagons over 2.5-3 years has slipped from Jul-Sep 2026 to next quarter; release is uncertain and affects bogie volumes.

rows.label: Preferential allotment proceeds
rows.why: About ₹100 crore fund raise from premier Indian funds has been announced, which will replace bill discounting used to fund working capital until it arrives.

tone.note: Management was confident on steel and power demand and on holding ₹300 plus crore FY27 guidance, but cautious on margins (8-10% normal PAT) and on the delayed railway mega wagon order; analysts pressed on H2 revenue ramp, working capital funding and PAT sustainability.
